definition: Family systems theory is a developmental perspective that understands an adolescent’s behavior in relation to how the family functions as a whole. In this view, changes in family functioning and a young person’s externalizing problems can influence each other over time.

reasons: The packet does not define family systems theory as a developmental perspective; it only says the study is based on family systems theory.

The phrase about understanding an adolescent’s behavior in relation to how the family functions as a whole is broader than the packet’s evidence, which only supports a reciprocal relationship between family functioning and externalizing problems in this study population.

The definition presents the theory as a general clinical/psychological account, but the packet provides only one study’s findings and should not be used to generalize the theory’s meaning beyond that evidence.
The packet does not explicitly support the claim that family systems theory is “a developmental perspective.” It only states “Based on family systems theory” and then reports a longitudinal study.

The packet supports longitudinal reciprocal associations between “family functioning” and “externalizing problems,” but the definition generalizes this to “an adolescent’s behavior” and “changes in family functioning… and a young person’s externalizing problems can influence each other over time” without explicit wording equivalent to “adolescent’s behavior” or a direct definitional statement connecting family systems theory to that developmental framing.
